title: Guide
intro: Everything you need to get started: follow the steps in order. The guide stays available during a session too.

prerequisites.title: Before you start
steps: Open Settings, paste your key into Anthropic API key and press Save. Without a key, Run analysis cannot produce the debrief.

Azure voice, voice commands and dictation need an Azure key and region (Azure Speech section); for the Azure voice also switch Status on. Otherwise engineer answers and the summary use the system voice.
Assign a controller button or a keyboard key in the Voice assistant section (button Assign): you use it to talk to the engineer.
This guide is always available: switching tab does not close your session.

accounts.title: Creating the Anthropic and Azure accounts
steps: Anthropic (analysis and engineer answers): create an account at platform.claude.com. It is the developer console, separate from any Claude chat subscription.
In the console open the billing section (Billing) and add prepaid credit: you pay by usage, so a small amount is enough to start.
Open API keys, create a key and copy it right away (it is not shown in full again). In Settings paste it into Anthropic API key and press Save.

Azure (voice, voice commands and dictation): sign up at azure.microsoft.com. Signing up needs a credit card, but according to Microsoft nothing is charged until you explicitly consent to a paid resource.

In the Azure portal create a Speech resource (Azure AI Speech, formerly Cognitive Services Speech): pick a region close to you and, if offered, the free tier, which includes a monthly quota of speech synthesis and recognition (current limits are in the Azure price list).

In the resource open Keys and Endpoint and copy one of the two keys. In Settings, Azure Speech section, paste it into Azure Speech key, pick the same Region as the resource and press Load voices: if the list loads, key and region are correct.

session.title: Starting a session
steps: Start your simulator and get on track, then press New session, pick the game (RaceRoom, Assetto Corsa EVO or Automobilista 2) and confirm with Open session. The chosen game must already be sending data.
Each pass over the line adds a lap to the table. Show telemetry plots brake, throttle and speed for that lap; invalid laps can be hidden with the filter above the table.
The session stays open until you press End session: recorded laps stay in the list.
To go back to a closed session open Session list and use Reopen session.

driving.title: Driving with the engineer
steps: While you drive the engineer stays quiet: it records laps and telemetry and detects anomalies (for example critical brake temperature, traction control, ABS, late braking), which the analysis then uses.
It learns your reference pace over the first 2 laps: after that it recognises deviations better.
With the Azure voice on, once you have enough laps the engineer says the stint is ready for analysis: that is the time to stop and press Run analysis.
To silence all voice use the toggle in the title bar, or Voice output in Settings. With voice off, the key to talk to the engineer does not respond either.

setup.title: Loading the setup
steps: Open Manage setups: the setup you load is linked to the following laps, and you can reuse setups already loaded for the same car and track.

RaceRoom: copy the setup in the game with CTRL+C and press Load from JSON. Assetto Corsa EVO: Select file and pick the .carsetup file. Automobilista 2: take screenshots of the setup screen and press Capture screenshots.

By voice: say acquire setup and the engineer asks for a name (RaceRoom from the clipboard, Automobilista 2 from the last 3 screenshots). With Assetto Corsa EVO it uses the latest file and its file name, without asking.
To link a setup to several laps already recorded, select them in the table and press Assign setup (N).

voice.title: Talking to the engineer
steps: The key is assigned in Settings, Voice assistant section: Controller or Keyboard. Assigning one removes the other.
Press it once, do not hold it: you hear the activation sound and have 5 seconds to speak. Recording stops by itself. With voice off the key does not respond.
While the engineer is processing or answering, further presses are ignored until the answer ends.
You can ask free questions (short radio-style answers) or give commands: new session RaceRoom, close session, analyze session, acquire setup. Saying the assistant's name gets a greeting.

analysis.title: Session analysis
steps: After a few laps press Run analysis: it calls the Claude API and produces a summary with suggested actions, which the engineer reads aloud.
For more detail press Show deep-dive analysis in the analysis: it is a second, longer call that adds telemetry, problems and a setup comparison.
Each analysis is its own version: with Comment you add a note, typed or dictated, and the engineer folds it in.
Setup advice comes one change at a time: apply it, drive a few laps and run the analysis again.

history.title: History, PDF and cleanup
steps: Session list gathers the sessions of all three games, with filters for game, car and track and sorting by date. Click a row to open its detail.
Inside a session, Export PDF saves the report with summary and deep-dive analysis.
You can delete single, selected or all sessions: laps, setups and analyses go with them, and it cannot be undone.
